I need to draft the root cause, executive summary, and assumptions sections while being careful not to restate the given figures as if I'd computed them myself or invent new impact numbers—I should describe the incident qualitatively instead.

For assumptions, I'll note that the flag change traces back to the provider's history with no deployment recorded (so the defect predates it), that the correlation between the revert and recovery supports causality, and that the affected path was account-page rendering, tying in the earlier deprioritized note about the monthly-spend feature.

assumptions: Causation is inferred from timing and from recovery after the flag was reverted, not proven: the errors began the minute the flag began rolling out and stopped when it was turned off.

The conclusion that no code release was involved rests on the change-event source returning zero production changes in the 24 hours before onset; if that source was incomplete, the alternative reading (a bad earlier deploy carrying the defect) is not excluded.
Only 36 minutes of logs before the alert and a 6-hour metrics window were examined; impact outside that window, and on any surface other than account page renders, was not checked.
The pre-incident ClientDisconnected errors are treated as ordinary background noise unrelated to this failure.
Recovery is judged from the service returning to its baseline error rate; no separate check was made that account page functionality was fully correct for every user afterwards.
The service was left running with the flag off; the underlying defect in src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py is still present and the proposed pull request has not been reviewed or merged.
input.executive_summary: On 24 September 2026, the online shop's account pages started failing at 09:33 UTC and were working normally again by 09:39 UTC — about six minutes. During that window a substantial share of shoppers trying to view their account page got an error instead; other parts of the shop were unaffected, and nothing was lost or corrupted — affected shoppers would have seen the page load correctly on a retry after recovery. The cause was a newly switched-on feature for monthly spending, which exposed a fault in the code that builds that part of the page. The automated on-call system picked up the alert, traced the failures to that feature being switched on, and switched it back off; the shop returned to its normal error levels immediately afterwards, which confirmed the diagnosis. A draft code fix for the underlying fault has been opened for engineers to review before the feature is enabled again.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was turned on for io-shop at 09:33 (partial rollout that minute — 176 off / 24 on — and fully on from 09:34), which opened a code path in `src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:626` that calls `max()` on an empty iterable; account page renders that hit that path raised `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty` until the flag was switched back off. No deploy or release was recorded in the 24 hours before onset, so the defect was latent in already-running code and the flag flip was the trigger, not the origin.
